candidates.spoken: Why 6% leftover heat nearly melted a reactor.
Cleanup lasted until 1993 and cost about $1 billion.
Coolant escaped, the core overheated and partially melted.
Reactors depend on continuous coolant flow to remove heat.
Coolant drained away, and the core partly melted.
But decay heat kept coming, about 6% of full power.
Nuclear reactor coolant pump failed because after a trip.
Replacing nuclear reactor coolant pump is not a simple purchase.
That's why cooling after shutdown matters as much as control.
The reactor continued to generate decay heat.
A relief valve opened to vent pressure, and stuck.
What stops if nuclear reactor coolant pump stops?
In 1979, Three Mile Island's reactor shut down automatically.

script.spoken: Why 6% leftover heat nearly melted a reactor. In 1979, Three Mile Island's reactor shut down automatically. But decay heat kept coming, about 6% of full power. A relief valve opened to vent pressure, and stuck. Operators believed it was closed. Coolant drained away, and the core partly melted. Cleanup lasted until 1993 and cost about $1 billion. That's why cooling after shutdown matters as much as control.
